name: TECAT 468 Single Channel
positioning: Single-channel wireless strain system for torque on shafts, flexplates, and driveline parts.
summary: The TECAT 468 Single Channel reads one strain gage bridge on a rotating or moving part and sends the data by radio to a base unit at your PC. It comes in 4,000, 6,000, and 8,000 Hz sampling versions. Its 16-bit A/D converter means you no longer send your strain range with the order so a gain resistor can be fitted before shipping. The remote transceiver weighs 6.5 g without its battery, and the base unit's four analog outputs feed your DAQ directly.

features: The 16-bit A/D converter covers the strain range without a factory gain setting, so you don't have to supply your strain range when you order. The earlier 12-bit design needed it to fit the right gain resistor before shipping.
The remote transceiver board measures 45 mm × 23 mm × 6 mm with mounting tabs and runs on a 3.7 V Li-Poly cell.
The base unit plugs into a PC USB port and carries the antenna, the transceiver, and four programmable 0 V to 5 V analog outputs for your DAQ.
Two independent shunt calibration legs, signal + and signal − to ground through 100 kΩ, let you check calibration in the field.
On-board data logging records events without a PC or DAQ connection.
Remote flash updates the firmware without removing the remote unit from the part under test.
Optional shaft enclosures protect the remote unit and battery from debris. The inductive charging version recharges the battery without exposing the USB port.
The system installs without altering the part under test and can be removed.
The kit ships in a carrying case with remote and base transceivers, antenna, battery, power adapters, cables, and TECAT Data Viewer software.

name: TECAT 468 Dual Channel
positioning: Two-channel wireless strain system for torque and thrust together, bending, and low-strain structures.
summary: The TECAT 468 Dual Channel reads two strain gage bridges from one remote unit, so a single installation measures two loads at once, such as torque and thrust on a propeller. It comes in 4,000, 6,000, and 8,000 Hz sampling versions, each with a choice of base unit: 4 analog outputs and a 30 m radio link, or 8 analog outputs and a 1,000 m radio link.

features: Two external strain gage inputs measure two loads at once on a rotating shaft, such as torque and axial load or two components of bending.
At 8 kHz the standard 400 mAh battery runs for up to 25 hours.
The radio link reaches 1,000 m line of sight with the 8-output base unit and 30 m with the 4-output base unit.
Four or eight analog output channels, depending on the base unit, each defined in TECAT Data Viewer, feed your DAQ directly.
The remote transceiver stores up to 30,000 samples on a trigger, so it captures high-speed events without a PC connection for download later.

An 18-bit A/D converter, two shunt calibration legs, and digital polarity reversal and zero are built in.
The system installs without altering the part under test and can be removed.

name: TECAT TC2-K
positioning: Two-channel wireless K-type thermocouple system for brake rotor temperature inside the wheel hub.
summary: The TECAT TC2-K reads two K-type thermocouples on a rotating wheel and sends the readings by radio to a base unit. It was designed for continuous brake rotor and spindle bearing temperature measurement and can be adapted to other applications. The remote unit sits in an 89 mm diameter by 42 mm enclosure on a mounting base made for each hub.
measures: Reference temperature at the remote unit, −25 °C to +125 °C
features: Two K-type thermocouple inputs with on-board channel amplification and on-board temperature referencing.
Digital thermocouple range is −40 °C to +1,000 °C; analog output range is −40 °C to +984 °C.
The remote unit is packaged in a standard 89 mm diameter by 42 mm enclosure on a mounting base designed for each wheel hub or application.
The base unit plugs into a PC USB port for TECAT Data Viewer, or into a power supply and DAQ through two 0 V to 5 V analog outputs.
Data rate is user selectable from 1 Hz to 10 Hz.
The remote draws 1.65 mA active with both thermocouples at 10 Hz and 25 µA inactive.
The system installs without altering the part under test and can be removed.

name: TECAT OEM Platform
category: Wireless sensor platform for OEM integration
positioning: Sensor fusion board and base unit for OEMs building wireless telemetry into products.
summary: The TECAT OEM Platform is a remote sensor fusion board, a base unit, and configuration software, based on TECAT test hardware and built for integration into an OEM's own product. Its first product, the TECAT LC100-PP, integrates into artificial lift pump jack load cells. The pre-production LC100-PP measures load at ±0.1% FS and 100 Hz over a 1,000 m link, with 13 months of battery life on a 19 Ah lithium D cell.
measures: Strain (torque, tension, compression, bending), including load cells
Temperature, including ambient temperature (optional on the TECAT LC100-PP)
Other quantities through MEMS sensors added to the remote unit
features: The remote sensor fusion board measures several quantities individually or together and is sized for integration into OEM products.
The TECAT LC100-PP base unit mounts on a DIN rail and delivers a ratiometric 2 mV/V ±0.02 analog output from a 5.000 V ±0.05 external excitation, so it connects to existing controls.
Data rate is 100 readings per second continuous and can be changed remotely from 1 Hz to 4 kHz.
One 3.6 V, 19 Ah lithium D cell powers the TECAT LC100-PP remote for 13 months at 100 Hz. The base unit LED turns steady red at 3.1 V; replace the battery within 2 weeks of that signal.
The remote unit is capable of achieving intrinsic safety certification (ATEX Zone 0), and the system is capable of achieving FCC, IC, and EU/CE wireless certification.
Available additions: a second analog output (voltage or current), digital USB output, battery voltage monitoring, over-the-air updates and configuration, and DC power isolation of the base unit.
The remote enters sleep mode when the base unit powers down, and data is available within 8 s of power-on.
Configuration software lets the OEM configure, calibrate, and display data from the system.
